overall: The AG found the Council violated the Law by posting conflicting access information for the June 23 and 24 budget hearings and by holding a June 22 meeting inaccessible on YouTube, but not on the other allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Council failed to properly and timely post notices for its June 22, 23, 24, and 25 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: With respect to all four meetings, we find that notice was timely posted to the municipal website.

allegations.summary: June 23 and 24 budget hearing notices conflicted: calendar entries listed Council Chambers, while the combined agenda said access was only by YouTube and cable.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by posting notices for its June 23 and 24 meetings that did not clearly inform the public of how it could access those meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the June 22 and June 25 notices were deficient.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, we find that for the June 22 and June 25 meetings, the calendar entries and agendas, taken together, provided all required information, and therefore notice was properly posted for these two meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council intentionally violated the Law in posting the meeting notices.
allegations.key_passage: After review of the evidence before us, we see no basis for finding an intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant implicitly challenged the start times of the June 23 and 24 budget hearings, which were split into public comment at 6:00 p.m. and hearing at 6:30 p.m.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find a violation of the Law with respect to the start time of the June 23 and 24 meetings, where the Council posted separate calendar events for public comment at 6:00 p.m. and the budget hearing at 6:30 p.m.

allegations.summary: The June 22 meeting was not streamed live on YouTube due to technical problems, though it was on Facebook and local access TV; the Council proceeded anyway.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Council violated the Law when it did not provide real-time access to its June 22 meeting via YouTube, which was the sole method of access listed on the notice for the June 22 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the June 25 Zoom meeting was not accessible to the public live on YouTube, showing a black error screen.
allegations.key_passage: Absent sufficient evidence to the contrary, we credit a public body’s version of events and find that the Council’s June 25 meeting was accessible to the public.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged Legislative Counsel and the City Clerk violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review allegations that Legislative Counsel or the City Clerk violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints raised additional allegations not arising under the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The complaints raise additional allegations that do not implicate the Open Meeting Law. We decline to review those allegations.

allegations.summary: General allegation that the City has consistently experienced technical difficulties streaming meetings live on YouTube, without identifying specific meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complaints do not identify any specific meetings that were inaccessible, other than the June 22 and June 25 meetings which we address herein, we decline to review the general allegation that the Council’s meetings have experienced technical problems.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
